title: Empiric Antibiotics — ED / ICU Syndromes
sources: Critical Vector — Empiric Therapy Guide Part II: ED/ICU & Critical Infections (IDSA-pattern reasoning)
IDSA practice guidelines: intra-abdominal infection, bacterial meningitis, infective endocarditis, febrile neutropenia, candidiasis, aspergillosis

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV ED/ICU & Critical Infections guide. Syndrome-level bug/drug/why structure; doses intentionally omitted; drug choices must reflect the local antibiogram.

summary: Syndrome-level empiric coverage for the infections that generate the 2am page. Coverage CLASS is shown; specific agents and doses must come from your institution's current antibiogram and the live guideline. De-escalate on culture data within 48–72 h.

body.text: This is a bug / drug / why reference for reasoning and study, not an order set. Doses are omitted deliberately. Confirm every regimen against the current guideline and your unit-specific antibiogram before treating a patient. In sepsis and the treat-before-confirmation syndromes, antibiotics within 1 hour of recognition is the quality metric — draw cultures in parallel, do not wait for the source to declare itself.

rows: Sepsis / septic shock, source unknown
Antipseudomonal beta-lactam (pip-tazo) + MRSA agent (vancomycin) ± antifungal if high-risk (recent surgery, TPN, prolonged ICU)
Broadest reasonable single-pass coverage — GPC incl. MRSA, GNR incl. Pseudomonas, anaerobes — while the source is localized
Abx within 1 h; 30 mL/kg crystalloid; blood cultures ×2 before abx if it does not delay therapy; source control in parallel; narrow within 48–72 h
Severe CAP (ICU-level)
Beta-lactam (ceftriaxone) + macrolide or respiratory fluoroquinolone; add MRSA agent (vancomycin / linezolid) if post-influenza or cavitary
Covers typical + atypical simultaneously; ICU disease no longer permits a narrow empiric guess
Add antipseudomonal / MRSA coverage in structural lung disease, recent hospitalization, or post-influenza necrotizing pneumonia. See the CAP module for the non-severe pathway.
HAP / VAP
Antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime / pip-tazo / meropenem) + MRSA agent (vancomycin) ± a second antipseudomonal if high resistance risk
Hospital flora skews to MDR GNR and MRSA — outpatient CAP regimens are inadequate
Base on the unit antibiogram; obtain a respiratory culture (ET aspirate or BAL); de-escalate aggressively once it returns
Aspiration pneumonia
Ampicillin-sulbactam (alt: clindamycin if PCN-allergic)
Oropharyngeal flora — anaerobes plus mixed GPC/GNR; anaerobic coverage is the key addition vs standard CAP
Infiltrate in dependent segments (RLL supine → posterior). Routine anaerobic coverage of pure chemical pneumonitis is overused.
Urosepsis / complicated UTI
Ceftriaxone; pip-tazo if resistant-flora risk (indwelling catheter, recent instrumentation, prior resistant organism)
IV agent with reliable GNR activity and renal-tract penetration
May present as delirium in the elderly. An obstructing infected stone is a urologic emergency — needs decompression, not just antibiotics.
Intra-abdominal infection (perforation / abscess)
Pip-tazo (alt: ceftriaxone + metronidazole)
Polymicrobial — enteric GNR + anaerobes — needs combined aerobic + anaerobic activity
Source control (drainage / surgery) is the primary intervention. Antibiotics alone will not cure an undrained abscess.
Necrotizing fasciitis
Vancomycin + pip-tazo + clindamycin — SURGICAL EMERGENCY
Broad coverage for mixed disease PLUS clindamycin to suppress exotoxin synthesis (protein-synthesis inhibition, independent of killing)
Pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading erythema, crepitus, bullae. Soft-tissue gas / LRINEC support but diagnosis is surgical. Emergent debridement is definitive.
Febrile neutropenia
Antipseudomonal beta-lactam monotherapy (cefepime or pip-tazo); add vancomycin only for line infection, SSTI signs, or instability
Pseudomonas coverage is non-negotiable given the fulminant course; monotherapy preferred absent specific risks
Fever (≥ 38.3 °C once, or ≥ 38.0 °C for 1 h) with ANC < 500. Abx within 1 h is a hard metric — do not wait for a source.
Adult bacterial meningitis (ICU / immunocompromised)
Vancomycin + ceftriaxone + ampicillin + dexamethasone
Ampicillin adds Listeria coverage for age > 50 or immunocompromise; steroid given with or before the first antibiotic dose
Do not delay antibiotics for imaging. CT before LP only if focal deficit, papilledema, or altered mentation — draw cultures and start empiric therapy if LP is delayed.
Infective endocarditis (acute, native valve)
Vancomycin + ceftriaxone. Prosthetic valve: add gentamicin + rifampin
Empiric cover for S. aureus (incl. MRSA), streptococci, enterococci pending speciation
Blood cultures ×3 from separate sites before abx; TTE → TEE; Duke criteria. IVDU → suspect right-sided (tricuspid) S. aureus disease with septic pulmonary emboli.
CLABSI
Vancomycin + antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime or pip-tazo)
CoNS / MRSA are most common; add GNR coverage since lines seed systemically before the organism is known
Paired cultures (peripheral + through-line) with differential time to positivity. Line removal for S. aureus, Candida, or persistent bacteremia.
Diabetic foot infection (moderate–severe)
Pip-tazo (± vancomycin if MRSA risk)
Chronic wounds are polymicrobial — GPC, GNR, anaerobes — once infection extends beyond superficial skin
Probe-to-bone test; plain films / MRI for osteomyelitis; deep-tissue culture beats a surface swab. Bone involvement changes the duration significantly.
Toxic shock syndrome (staph / strep)
Vancomycin (or oxacillin) + clindamycin
Clindamycin suppresses TSST-1 / exotoxin synthesis independent of killing — a critical adjunct beyond the beta-lactam / glycopeptide
Clinical diagnosis (CDC criteria); blood cultures often negative in staph TSS (toxin-mediated). Find and remove the source — retained tampon, wound packing, abscess.
Candidemia / invasive candidiasis (septic ICU patient)
Echinocandin (micafungin / caspofungin)
Fungicidal, covers azole-resistant species — preferred first-line in the unstable ICU patient pending speciation

Persistent fever / shock despite broad antibacterials in a line-bearing, post-op, or TPN-dependent patient. Dilated fundoscopy to exclude endophthalmitis. Remove / exchange the line. Step down to fluconazole once susceptible and stable.
Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
Voriconazole (alt: isavuconazole — fewer interactions / less QT effect)
First-line per IDSA for reliable Aspergillus activity and CNS penetration
Halo or air-crescent sign on CT; serum galactomannan, BAL galactomannan more sensitive. Mortality high even treated — start on radiographic suspicion.
Mucormycosis (rhino-orbital-cerebral)
Liposomal amphotericin B, high-dose + EMERGENT surgical debridement
Amphotericin is the reliably active agent against Mucorales; azoles (fluconazole, voriconazole) have NO activity — the key distinction from Aspergillus

Poorly-controlled DKA or profound neutropenia; black necrotic eschar on palate / turbinates, proptosis, CN deficits. Broad non-septate right-angle-branching hyphae. Debridement is co-equal with the drug.
Pneumocystis pneumonia (PJP)
High-dose TMP-SMX + corticosteroids if PaO₂ < 70 or elevated A–a gradient
TMP-SMX has the best-evidenced outcomes; steroids blunt the inflammatory response to organism die-off that otherwise worsens hypoxemia
Subacute dyspnea, dry cough, fever in AIDS (CD4 < 200) or profound immunosuppression. Bilateral ground-glass, elevated LDH. Steroids start WITH or BEFORE the first antimicrobial dose.
Severe influenza (viral ARDS)
Oseltamivir (IV peramivir if enteral route unusable) + lung-protective ventilation
Antiviral is indicated regardless of symptom-onset timing once hospitalized with severe disease
Watch for post-influenza necrotizing S. aureus (incl. MRSA) pneumonia — add empiric MRSA coverage if suspected.
HSV / VZV encephalitis
IV acyclovir, high-dose — start empirically, treat before confirmation
Untreated mortality is very high and the drug's toxicity is low enough to justify empiric use on suspicion alone
MRI temporal-lobe change (HSV); CSF PCR for HSV/VZV; EEG PLEDs in HSV. Monitor renal function and hydrate — acyclovir crystallizes in the tubules at high doses.
Severe COVID-19 pneumonia / ARDS
Remdesivir + dexamethasone ± immunomodulator (tocilizumab / baricitinib) per severity
Remdesivir shortens recovery in hypoxemic inpatients; dexamethasone reduces mortality specifically in those needing O₂ or ventilation
Timing matters — steroids given early in the viral-replication phase (before hypoxemia) may worsen outcomes.
CMV reactivation (transplant / critically ill)
Ganciclovir (or valganciclovir PO if tolerating enteral route)
Treat end-organ disease or high viral load in the immunosuppressed — not incidental low-level viremia
Pneumonitis, colitis (GI bleed / diarrhea). Trend CMV PCR; tissue biopsy + IHC for definitive end-organ diagnosis. Ganciclovir causes significant myelosuppression.

body.text: Rare & time-critical — recognition is the rate-limiting step

For meningococcemia, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and inhalational anthrax, the antibiotic is not the hard part — recognizing the syndrome and giving the drug before confirmation is. Suspected bioterrorism-relevant pathogens (anthrax, plague, tularemia, botulism) are reportable to public health immediately.

rows: Meningococcemia / Waterhouse-Friderichsen
Ceftriaxone immediately + hydrocortisone if adrenal-hemorrhage shock
Fever + rapidly spreading petechial / purpuric rash + hypotension + DIC; collapse within hours
Give antibiotics on clinical suspicion — do not wait for LP or culture.
Rocky Mountain spotted fever
Doxycycline — start empirically, at any age
Fever, headache, myalgias → maculopapular rash on wrists / ankles spreading to palms / soles
Doxycycline is the only agent proven to reduce mortality; this overrides usual pediatric tetracycline avoidance. Serology is often negative in week 1.
Inhalational / systemic anthrax
Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin + linezolid + a third agent (multi-drug IV) + antitoxin (raxibacumab / obiltoxaximab) if available
Flu-like prodrome → abrupt respiratory failure + widened mediastinum + shock
Bactericidal + protein-synthesis inhibitor to kill AND halt toxin production; antitoxin neutralizes circulating toxin. Report to public health.
Cutaneous anthrax
Ciprofloxacin or doxycycline (oral)
Painless papule → vesicle → black eschar with non-pitting edema; animal-hide / wool / livestock exposure
Do NOT debride the eschar — it resolves with antibiotics; systemic spread is the real risk.
Plague (bubonic)
Streptomycin or gentamicin (alt: doxycycline, fluoroquinolone)
Sudden fever + intensely painful swollen node (bubo); flea / rodent exposure in an endemic region
Bipolar 'safety-pin' GN coccobacillus on bubo aspirate. Treat empirically — can progress to septicemic or pneumonic plague.
Plague (pneumonic)
Streptomycin / gentamicin or IV fluoroquinolone + DROPLET isolation
Fulminant pneumonia with hemoptysis within 1–2 days of exposure
The only plague form transmissible human-to-human — droplet precautions immediately, notify public health. Uniformly fatal untreated.
Tularemia
Streptomycin or gentamicin (alt: doxycycline / ciprofloxacin for milder disease)
Painful skin ulcer + tender regional nodes after tick / rabbit / deer-fly exposure; hunters, trappers
Intracellular organism — needs an agent with intracellular penetration. Culture is hazardous — notify the lab of suspicion.
Botulism
Botulinum antitoxin — antibiotics are NOT primary; AVOID aminoglycosides
Descending symmetric flaccid paralysis (diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia), afebrile, no sensory deficit
Toxin-mediated; antitoxin neutralizes unbound toxin. Aminoglycosides potentiate neuromuscular blockade. Infant botulism uses human BIG, not equine antitoxin.
Leptospirosis / Weil's disease
Doxycycline (mild) or penicillin G / ceftriaxone (severe)
Biphasic fever + myalgias + conjunctival suffusion → jaundice, renal failure, hemorrhage; freshwater / animal-urine exposure
Elevated bilirubin with only mildly elevated transaminases distinguishes it from viral hepatitis. Consider in returning travelers after rafting / flooding.

items: Broaden deliberately, de-escalate on purpose — plan the narrowing from the first order, and reassess at 48–72 h against culture data.
Source control (drainage, debridement, line removal, decompression of an obstructed tract) is co-equal with — often more important than — the antibiotic.
Clindamycin or linezolid is added to a beta-lactam in necrotizing fasciitis and toxic shock specifically to shut down exotoxin synthesis, not for extra killing.
Azoles have no activity against Mucorales — if the CT and the host (DKA, neutropenia) fit mucormycosis, the drug is amphotericin, not voriconazole.
Steroids in PJP and in severe COVID go WITH or BEFORE the first antimicrobial dose; in bacterial meningitis, dexamethasone goes with or before the first antibiotic.
